newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong to shut central harbour for handover.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong to shut central harbour for handover.

text.p: Hong Kong is to close the main channel of the world's busiest port for safety and security reasons as it turns over Victoria Harbour to celebrations of its return to Chinese rule next week, marine police said on Tuesday.
They said the harbour would be sealed off in the Central and Wanchai areas to all but specially exempted vessels from the afternoon of June 30 until the early hours of July 2.
Ships would have to pass around the southern side of Hong Kong Island instead, a police spokesman said.
Hong Kong reverts to China at the stroke of midnight on June 30, ending 156 years of British colonial rule.
Victoria Harbour will be the stage for a series of spectacular fireworks and laser displays launched from a fleet of barges strung across the waterway.
Britain's Prince Charles will sail out from there aboard the royal yacht Britannia early on July 1 after formally handing back the colony to Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
Cross-harbour ferries are to halt services during the firework shows on Monday and Tuesday nights.
